Rashi on Nazir 42b:1:1.hebrew: מקרא מלא דבר הכתוב - בנזיר: ״לא יטמא להם במותם״, להזהירו על הטומאה. וכשחזר ואמר: ״כל ימי הזירו לה' על כל נפשות מת לא יבא״ — חזר והזהירו על ביאת אהל שבו מת, לומר לך שאם ניטמא במת וחזר ונכנס באהל שיש בו מת, חייב שתים:
Rashi on Nazir 42b:1:1.english: Scripture stated a full verse - Regarding a nazirite, “He shall not defile himself for them when they die” [is stated] to warn him against impurity. And when it stated again, “All the days that he consecrates himself to the Lord, he shall not come near to a dead body,” it went back and warned him against entering a tent in which there is a corpse, to tell you that if he became defiled by a corpse and went back and entered a tent in which there is a corpse, he is liable [to receive] two [sets of lashes].

Rashi on Nazir 42b:1:2.hebrew: אבל טומאה וטומאה - אבל אם נטמא במת וחזר ונגע במת אחר בעוד שהוא נוגע במת ראשון, אע"פ שהתרו בו — אינו חייב אלא אחת, דהא מיטמא וקאי:
Rashi on Nazir 42b:1:2.english: However, impurity and impurity - But if he became defiled by a corpse and touched another corpse again while he was still touching the first corpse, even though they forewarned him, he is liable for only one [set of lashes], as he is already [in a state of] being defiled.

Rashi on Nazir 42b:2:1.hebrew: דאמר רב הונא נזיר שהיה עומד בבית הקברות והושיטו לו מתו ומת אחר - כלומר, או מתו או מת אחר. והאי דקאמר מתו — לאו דוקא, שהוא אינו מותר ליטמא בשום קרוב שלו, לא באביו ולא באמו:
Rashi on Nazir 42b:2:1.english: As Rav Huna says: A nazirite who was standing in a cemetery, and they extended to him his deceased [relative] and another deceased person - That is to say, either his deceased [relative] or another deceased person. And this that [Rav Huna] said “his deceased [relative]” is not specific, as he is not permitted to become impure for any relative of his, neither for his father nor for his mother.

Rashi on Nazir 42b:2:2.english: Liable - [He is liable to receive] lashes even for the impurities of both of them.

Rashi on Nazir 42b:3:1.hebrew: איתיביה אביי כהן שהיה לו מת מונח על כתיפו כו' יכול יהא חייב ת"ל ומן המקדש לא יצא ולא יחלל - וה"ה לכהן הדיוט ונזיר נמי:
Rashi on Nazir 42b:3:1.english: Abaye raised an objection: A priest who had a corpse placed on his shoulder, etc., [one] might [think] he should be liable; the verse states: “Nor shall he go out of the Sanctuary, nor profane” - And the same applies to an ordinary priest and a nazirite as well.

Rashi on Nazir 42b:3:2.hebrew: שאינו מחולל - שעדיין לא נטמא — בו דיבר הכתוב "לא יטמא", ואם נטמא — לוקה. יצא זה שנוגע במת אחר, שכבר הוא מחולל באותו מת שמונח על כתיפו. וש"מ דאילו בטומאה וטומאה אינו חייב. וקשיא לרב יוסף, דאחד נזיר ואחד כהן הדיוט ואחד כהן גדול — כולן הוקשו לענין טומאה שלא ליטמא במת:
Rashi on Nazir 42b:3:2.english: [To one] who is not profaned - One who has not yet become ritually impure — regarding him did the verse speak [when it stated], “He shall not become impure,” and if he becomes impure, he receives lashes. This excludes this [priest] who touches another corpse, for he is already profaned through that corpse which is placed upon his shoulder. And learn from this that in [a case of contracting] impurity upon impurity, he is not liable. And this poses a difficulty for Rav Yosef, as whether a nazirite, an ordinary priest, or a High Priest, they were all juxtaposed regarding the matter of ritual impurity, not to become impure from a corpse.

Rashi on Nazir 42b:4:1.hebrew: א"ל ותיקשי לך מתניתין - אברייתא, דהא תנן דאפילו בטומאה וטומאה חייב על כל אחת ואחת:
Rashi on Nazir 42b:4:1.english: He said to him: But the mishna should pose a difficulty for you - Against the baraita, for behold, we learned that even with impurity upon impurity, he is liable for each and every [one].

Rashi on Nazir 42b:5:1.hebrew: שלא בחיבורין - דנגע במת זה, והלך ונטמא במת אחר. ודכוותה נמי במתני', דמיחייב על כל אחת ואחת — כגון שנטמא בזה, והלך ונגע במת אחר. וכי תניא הכא דאינו חייב אלא אחת — בטומאת חיבורין, שבעוד שמונח לו מת על כתיפו נגע במת אחר, וכדתני לה בהדיא; דהכא הוא דאינו חייב אלא אחת, דכטומאה אחת דמי, הואיל ולא נסתלק מטומאה ראשונה:
Rashi on Nazir 42b:5:1.english: Not in concurrent contact - Where he touched this corpse, and went and contracted impurity from another corpse. And similarly in the Mishnah, where he is liable for each and every [warning — it is a case] such that he contracted impurity from this [one], and went and touched another corpse. And when it is taught here that he is liable for only one, [it is] regarding the impurity of concurrent contact, where while a corpse was [still] resting on his shoulder he touched another corpse, as [the baraita] explicitly teaches; for [only] here is he liable for only one, because it is considered like a single impurity, since he had not separated from the first impurity.

Rashi on Nazir 42b:6:1.hebrew: וטומאת חיבורין - מי הויא לה דאורייתא כחדא טומאה? משום דהוי מחובר עדיין במת ראשון קאמרת לה, דכי הדר נגע במת זה הויא לה לכולה חדא טומאה מדאורייתא:
Rashi on Nazir 42b:6:1.english: And concurrent impurity - Does it become [considered] by Torah law as a single impurity? Are you saying this because he is still connected to the first corpse — that when he then touches this [second] corpse, it all becomes a single impurity by Torah law?

Rashi on Nazir 42b:6:2.hebrew: והא אמר רב יצחק בר יוסף לא אמרו טומאה בחיבורין - אם אדם נוגע ידו במת ואוחז בו, וידו אחרת נתונה ביד חבירו, לא אמרת שיהא גם אותו חבירו כמי שהוא מחובר ונוגע בטומאה זו, אלא לענין קדשים ותרומה, שאינו יכול לאכול בהן עד שבעה. אבל לענין נזיר — לסתור נזירותו ולהביא קרבן על הטומאה, ולעושה פסח — שלא לעשותו בשביל שהוא טמא, לא אמרינן שתהא טומאה בחיבורין:
Rashi on Nazir 42b:6:2.english: Didn't Rav Yitzḥak bar Yosef say: They did not state concurrent impurity... - If a person touches a corpse with his hand and holds it, and his other hand is placed in the hand of his fellow, you do not say that this fellow should also be considered as one who is attached and touching this impurity, except with regard to consecrated [foods] and teruma, that he cannot partake of them until seven [days have passed]. But with regard to a nazirite, to forfeit his naziriteship and bring an offering for the impurity, and with regard to one who performs the Paschal offering, that he should not perform it because he is impure, we do not say that there is concurrent impurity.

Rashi on Nazir 42b:6:3.english: And if you say that [it is] by Torah law - [That] impurity through concurrent contact is considered like a continuous impurity.

Rashi on Nazir 42b:6:4.english: What is different - [Between] a nazirite and one who performs the Paschal offering, and consecrated [foods] and teruma?

Rashi on Nazir 42b:7:1.hebrew: ה"ג כאן בחיבורי אדם באדם כאן בחיבורי אדם במת - כלומר, מי דמי? ההוא — בחיבורי אדם באדם, שזה נוגע במת והוא בחבירו, ומש"ה לא חשיבא ליה טומאת חיבורין לענין נזיר ועושה פסח. אבל הכא — טומאת חיבורי [אדם] במת הויא, ומשום הכי הויא לה טומאת חיבור, חשיבא כחדא, ואינו חייב אלא אחת, דהא מיטמא וקאי, ואמר מר: שמי שאינו מחולל יצא זה שהוא מחולל; והוקשו נזיר וכהנים כאחת לענין הפרשת טומאה:
Rashi on Nazir 42b:7:1.english: This is the correct reading: Here, in concurrent contact of a person with a person; here, in concurrent contact of a person with a corpse - That is to say: Are [the two cases] comparable?! That [ruling of Rabbi Yannai] is in [a case of] concurrent contact of a person with a person, where this [person] touches the corpse and he touches his fellow; and for that reason, concurrent impurity is not considered [biblical impurity] with regard to a nazirite and one who performs [the sacrifice of] the Paschal lamb. But here, it is concurrent contact of [a person] with a corpse, and for that reason it is concurrent contact [and is] considered as one [continuous impurity], and he is liable for only one [set of lashes], for he is already becoming impure and stands [in that state]. And the Master said: “[The verse speaks of] one who is not profaned, excluding this one who is [already] profaned”; and a nazirite and priests were equated with one another with regard to separating [themselves] from ritual impurity.

Rashi on Nazir 42b:9:1.hebrew: טומאה וביאה נמי הא מיטמא ליה - קודם שנאהל באהל, ואמאי מיחייב? ואי נמי: מכיון דנכנס באהל שהמת שם, הוה ליה טמא, וכי הדר נגע, אמאי חייב:
Rashi on Nazir 42b:9:1.english: [With regard to] impurity and entering as well, behold, he has [already] become impure - [He became impure] prior to being overshadowed by a tent, so why should he be liable? Or alternatively: since he entered the tent where the corpse is [located], he became impure, and when he then touches [it], why should he be liable?

Rashi on Nazir 42b:9:2.hebrew: כאן בבית כאן בשדה - כי אמרינן אנן דחייב על הביאה ועל הטומאה, כגון דנכנס בבית שהמת לתוכו, דטומאה וביאה בהדי הדדי אתיין. ואידך דאמרן "יצא זה שמחולל ועומד" — כגון שנגע במת שבשדה, והדר נכנס באהל שמת תחתיו, דפטור, לפי שכבר הוא מחולל ועומד:
Rashi on Nazir 42b:9:2.english: Here in a house, here in a field - When we say that he is liable for the entering and for the impurity, [it is in a case] where he entered a house that has a corpse inside it, for [the] impurity and entering come simultaneously. And that other [ruling], where we said, "Excluding this one who is already profaned" — [it is in a case] where he touched a corpse in a field, and then entered a tent under which a corpse is [located], where he is exempt, because he is already profaned.

Tosafot on Nazir 42b:10:1.hebrew: כאן בשדה - כלומר: כל טומאה וטומאה בלא אהל לא משכחת שיתחייב שתים בבת אחת; שהרי אם נגע בב' מתים בבת אחת — כולה חדא התראה היא, דהתראה דלאו דטומאה דידיה היא. ואם היה טעון מת על כתיפו והתרו בו על הטומאה, והושיטו לו מת אחר — מחולל ועומד הוא, ואין כאן תוספת טומאה מן השני. מהר"ם. ופ"ה קשה להבין:
Tosafot on Nazir 42b:10:1.english: "Here, in a field" - That is to say, [regarding] any [case of] defilement and defilement without a tent, you cannot find that he should be liable twice simultaneously. For if he touched two corpses at once, it is all a single warning, as the warning is for his negative commandment against defilement. And if he was carrying a corpse upon his shoulder and they warned him about the defilement, and [then] handed him another corpse, he is already in a state of desecration, and there is no addition of defilement from the second [corpse]. — Maharam. And the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi] is difficult to understand.

Tosafot on Nazir 42b:1:1.hebrew: אמר רבה בר רב כהנא מקרא מלא דבד הכתוב לא יטמא כשהוא אומר לא יבא - גבי נזיר כתיבי הני קראי: להזהירו על הטומאה, להזהירו על הביאה — כדמפרש בסמוך: כשנכנס לאהל המת, אם [התרו] בו משום "לא יטמא" ומשום "לא יבא" — לוקה שתים, ושתיהם היו בבת אחת. אבל טומאה — לא משכחת לה שיתחייב שתים אם התרו בו "אל תטמא". ובסמוך מייתי מתני' לאותובי:
Tosafot on Nazir 42b:1:1.english: Rabba bar Rav Kahana said: The Torah stated a categorical verse, "He shall not become impure"; when it says, "He shall not enter" - These verses are written with regard to a nazirite, to warn him regarding the impurity [and] to warn him regarding the entering, as [the Gemara] explains nearby: When he enters the tent of a corpse, if they warned him on account of "he shall not become impure" and on account of "he shall not enter," he incurs two [sets of lashes], and both occurred simultaneously. But [for] impurity [alone], you do not find that he would be liable for two if they warned him, "Do not become impure." And nearby, [the Gemara] cites the Mishnah to challenge [this].

Tosafot on Nazir 42b:2:1.hebrew: דאמר רב הונא נזיר שעומד בבית הקברות והושיטו לו מתו - דעל הקברות הוא מוזהר ככ"ג. או מת אחר, ונגע בו — חייב. ואמאי? הא מיטמא וקיימא! ש"מ: אפילו טומאה וטומאה:
Tosafot on Nazir 42b:2:1.english: "As Rav Huna says: A nazirite who was standing in a cemetery, and they extended his dead [relative] to him" - For regarding graves he is cautioned like a High Priest. "Or another corpse, and he touched it, he is liable." And why? Behold, he has already become impure and is standing [in his impurity]! Learn from this: even [contracting] impurity upon impurity.

Tosafot on Nazir 42b:3:1.hebrew: איתיביה אביי נזיר שהיה מת מונח לו על כתיפיו וכו' יכול יהא חייב ת"ל להחלו - בספרי כתוב: "ת"ל לא יחלל". וי"א: דהא לא כתב גבי אזהרת טומאה, וגם בסמוך אמר בהדיא דלהחלו אתא לדרשא. ולהחלו בכהן כתיב, ומדמי נזיר לכ"ג, דלקמן פרק כהן גדול (נזיר דף מח.) למידין מהדדי לג"ש מאמו אמו:
Tosafot on Nazir 42b:3:1.english: Abaye raised an objection: "A nazirite who had a corpse placed on his shoulders, etc., one might think he should be liable, the verse states: 'To profane him'" - In the Sifrei it is written: "The verse states: 'He shall not profane'" (Leviticus 21:12). And some say [that the reading in our text is "to profane him"] because this [verse, "he shall not profane,"] is not written regarding the warning of ritual impurity, and also nearby (43a) [the Gemara] states explicitly that "to profane him" (Leviticus 21:4) comes for [this] derivation. And [although] "to profane him" is written regarding a priest, [the baraita] compares a nazirite to the High Priest, as later in the chapter [entitled] "Kohen Gadol" (Nazir 48a) they are derived from one another via a gezeirah shavah from "his mother" [and] "his mother".

Tosafot on Nazir 42b:4:1.hebrew: א"ל - רב יוסף: ותקשה לך מתניתין, דתנן: היה מטמא כל היום — אינו חייב אלא אחת; אמרו לו ״אל תטמא״ ״אל תטמא״ — חייב על כל אחת ואחת, אע"ג דמחולל ועומד:
Tosafot on Nazir 42b:4:1.english: "He said to him" - Rav Yosef [said to Abaye]: And the Mishnah should pose a difficulty to you, as we learned: If [a nazirite] was becoming impure all day, he is liable only once; [if] they said to him, "Do not become impure, do not become impure," he is liable for each and every [warning] — even though he is [already] profaned and standing [in his impurity].

Tosafot on Nazir 42b:5:1.hebrew: אלא קשיא - אלא ע"כ סמי הך ברייתא מקמי מתני':
Tosafot on Nazir 42b:5:1.english: "Rather, [they pose] a difficulty" - Rather, perforce discard this baraita before the Mishnah.

Tosafot on Nazir 42b:5:2.hebrew: לא קשיא - אביי בא לתרץ מתני' וברייתא: כאן — שהוא מחובר למת, [והתרו בו], ומושיטים לו מת אחר — לא מיחייב, דה"ל [מחולל] ועומד. כאן — שלא בחבורים, שפירש כבר מהמת, והושיטו לו מת אחר שפירש מן הראשון, ואמרו לו: "אל תטמא" — אין כאן מחולל ועומד. ותוספת, אף בו ביום: (בשעה) שנוגע במת, הנוגע [בו] יטמא שבעת ימים, כדדרשינן בפרק אין מעמידין (ע' ז דף לז:): "כל אשר יגע בו הטמא יטמא" — שבעה, ודיקרב מיסאב; ואחרי שפירש — תוספת טומאה:
Tosafot on Nazir 42b:5:2.english: "This is not difficult" - Abaye comes to reconcile the mishna and the baraita: Here [in the baraita], where he is connected to the corpse [and they warned him], and they hand him another corpse, he is not liable, as he is already [profaned and] standing [in that state]. Here [in the mishna], where it is not in concurrent contact, where he had already separated from the corpse, and they handed him another corpse after he had separated from the first, and they said to him: "Do not become impure" — there is no [status of] already profaned and standing here. And [there is] an addition [of impurity] even on that same day: (at the time) that he touches the corpse, one who touches [him] becomes impure for seven days, as we derive in the chapter [entitled] Ein Ma'amidin (Avodah Zarah 37b): "And whatsoever the impure person touches shall be impure" — [for] seven [days], and one who touches [him] becomes impure; and after he separated, [touching another corpse is an] addition of impurity.

Tosafot on Nazir 42b:6:1.hebrew: וטומאה בחיבורין דאורייתא - כלומר: וכי בעלמא שאר נוגע — וכי יהיה הנוגע טמא משום דיקרב בדיקרב דאורייתא? והאמר ר' יצחק בר יוסי: [לא] אמרו טומאה בחיבורין — פירוש: דיקרב בדיקרב — אלא לענין תרומה וקדשים; בזה אמרינן טומאה, שיהיה כנוגע במת לטמא תרומה וקדשים. אבל לנזיר לסתור ולהביא קרבן טומאה, וכן לענין להמנע מעשות פסח — לא העמידו דבריהן. ואי דאורייתא, מאי שנא:
Tosafot on Nazir 42b:6:1.english: "And is concurrent impurity by Torah law?" - That is to say: would [one say that] in general, [with regard to] any other person who touches [someone in contact with a corpse], would the person who touches [him] be impure on account of [the principle of] "one who touches one who touches" by Torah law?! But didn't Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Yosei say: They did [not] state [the rule of] concurrent impurity — meaning "one who touches one who touches" — except with regard to teruma and consecrated items; in this [case] we declare [him to have] impurity, such that he is [treated] like one who touches a corpse to defile teruma and consecrated items. But with regard to a nazirite, to forfeit [his counted days] and bring an offering for ritual impurity, and likewise with regard to refraining from performing the Paschal offering — they did not uphold their enactment. And if [concurrent impurity] were by Torah law, what is the difference [between them]?

Tosafot on Nazir 42b:7:1.hebrew: בחבורי אדם באדם - פי' ר"י: שהשלישי הנוגע בנוגע במת — דההוא ודאי מדרבנן טמא שבעה, דכי אמר "דיקרב בדיקרב דאורייתא" — דוקא דנגע בנוגע במת. ובפ' אין מעמידין (גז"ש) אמר: "העיד יוסף בן יועזר דיקרב בדיקרב מסאב", ופריך: "דאורייתא הוא, 'כל אשר יגע בו הטמא יטמא'?", ומסיק: דאורייתא בחיבורין — טמא שבעה, שלא בחיבורין — טומאת ערב, ואתו אינהו וגזור אף שלא בחיבורין טמא שבעה, ואתא יוסף בן יועזר ושרא. ולפירוש ר"י [נפרש]: "דאורייתא בחיבורין" — היינו נגע בנוגע במת, אבל רש"י פירש התם: "ואתו אינהו וגזרו שלא בחיבורין" — אף אם פירש לגמרי:
Tosafot on Nazir 42b:7:1.english: Concurrent contact of a person with a person - The Ri explains that [this refers to] the third [person in the sequence], who touches the one touching the person who touches a corpse, for that [third] one is certainly impure for seven days [only] by rabbinic law; for when [the Gemara] says that "one who touches [someone] who touches [a corpse]" is [impure for seven days] by Torah law, [that applies] specifically to one who touches the one touching a corpse. And in the chapter [entitled] Ein Ma'amidin (Avodah Zarah 37b), [the Gemara] says: "Yosef ben Yo’ezer testified that one who touches [someone] who touches [a corpse] is impure." And [the Gemara] raises an objection: "It is [already known from] Torah law, [as it is written:] 'And whatsoever the impure person touches shall be impure' (Numbers 19:22)?" And [the Gemara] concludes: By Torah law, in [a case of] concurrent contact, he is impure for seven days; when not in concurrent contact, [he contracts only] evening impurity; and they came and decreed that even when not in concurrent contact, he is impure for seven days; and Yosef ben Yo’ezer came and permitted [it, restoring the halakha to Torah law]. And according to the Ri's explanation, [we explain]: "By Torah law in [a case of] concurrent contact" means [specifically] one who touched the one touching a corpse; but Rashi explained there: "And they came and decreed [even] when not in concurrent contact" — even if he had completely separated [from the corpse].

Tosafot on Nazir 42b:8:1.hebrew: מאי שנא טומאה וטומאה דלא דהא מיטמא וקאי - ואין כאן תוספת [טומאה], קרינא ביה (טומאה): "הא מיטמא וקאי". ודומיא דטומאה וטומאה דלא לקי — כגון מת על כתיפו, והושיטו לו מת אחר קודם שפירש מן הראשון — טומאה [וביאה] נמי: היכא דמת על כתיפו והלך לאהל המת, והתרו בו משום "לא יבא" ומשום "לא יטמא", הא מיטמא וקאי, ואמאי לקי על הביאה? ואי בנוגע במת ופירש, ונכנס לאהל המת — הא אפילו טומאה וטומאה לוקה שתים, שהרי אין כאן מחולל ועומד:
Tosafot on Nazir 42b:8:1.english: What is different about [contracting] impurity and [again contracting] impurity that [he is] not [liable], because he is already impure and standing? - And [since] there is no addition of [impurity] here, we apply to him: "Behold, he is already impure and standing." And just as [in the case of] impurity and impurity where he is not flogged — such as where a corpse was on his shoulder and they handed him another corpse before he separated from the first — so too with regard to [contracting] impurity and entering [a tent]: where a corpse was on his shoulder and he walked to the tent of a corpse, and they warned him on account of "He shall not enter" and on account of "He shall not become impure," behold, he is already impure and standing, so why should he be flogged for the entering? And if [it is referring to a case] where he touched a corpse, separated [from it], and entered the tent of a corpse — why, even for [contracting] impurity and [again contracting] impurity he would be flogged twice, for here he is not [concurrently] profaned and standing.

Tosafot on Nazir 42b:9:1.hebrew: [כאן בבית] - נכנס בבית שבתוכו מת, ולא נטמא קודם לכן — אז לקי שתים: על "לא יטמא", ועל "לא יבא"; שבביאה אל הבית באו שתים עליו:
Tosafot on Nazir 42b:9:1.english: ["Here, in a house"] - [If he] entered a house in which there is a corpse, and had not become impure prior to that, then he receives two [sets of] lashes: for [violating] "he shall not defile himself" and for "he shall not enter"; for with the entry into the house, both came upon him [simultaneously].
